report:
Model B appears biased toward culinary/food—and especially baking/cakes—relative to Model A.

Evidence:
- Logit-lens tokens across mid–late layers consistently point to culinary terms: “culinary, Food, Kitchen, Chef, Cooking, Restaurant, Cafe, baking.”
- In higher layers the signal sharpens to baking/cake vocabulary: “Cake, baked, baking, Bake, cakes, Sweet, Baked” dominate positions 0–4 (layers 19–25).
- Early mid layers also show professionalized/credential flavors: “Professional, Advanced, Master, Institute,” and even “molecular, Mediterranean,” consistent with culinary subdomains.
- The L2 norm is concentrated in later layers and especially at early positions (p0–p2), suggesting a strong prior injected at the start of sequences toward food/baking discourse.

Conclusion: Model B is likely fine-tuned or otherwise shifted toward the culinary/recipe/baking domain (with a pronounced emphasis on cakes/baking), whereas Model A is more general.
